sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Pike County, Missouri?
sections.html:
The Pike County Collector of Revenue, Tara J. Eskew, bills and collects real estate and personal property tax from the courthouse in Bowling Green. The office sits at 115 West Main, Bowling Green, MO 63334, and the number is 573-324-3281. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a closure from 12:00 to 1:00 that is lifted during tax season.

The collector says it handles more than $20 million a year and passes the money to schools, roads, cities, fire districts, levees and drainage districts every month. It collects what the assessor's records show and cannot change a value, a legal description or a mailing address. Those fixes go to the Pike County Assessor at 573-324-3261. See the collector's general tax page for the current wording.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Pike County itself?
sections.html:
Pike County sits on Missouri's eastern edge, with the Mississippi River as its border and Bowling Green as the county seat. The county was organized on December 14, 1818, and it covers about 670 square miles of land. Its cities are Bowling Green, Clarksville, Curryville, Frankford and Louisiana, and its public school districts include Bowling Green R-I, Louisiana R-II and Pike County R-III at Clarksville.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page shows a county that is rural and settled mostly by owners. It also shows how modest the housing market is next to the Kansas City side of the state.

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 17,955, which is 26.2 people per square mile (2020).
  • Housing units in 2025: 7,682, with 73.3 percent of occupied homes owner-occupied (2020 to 2024).
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $146,000, and median gross rent: $778.
  • Median household income: $54,989, with 21.1 percent of residents aged 65 or older.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 20.

A low median value means that a single delinquent year can be a large share of what a house is worth, so the timing of the bill matters more here than the rate itself. Source: Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: When are Pike County tax bills mailed and due?
sections.html:
Statements go out on the first day of November. If yours has not arrived by mid-November, call the collector, because a missing bill does not cancel the tax or the late charges. Payment is on time when it is postmarked by December 31, and anything postmarked later is returned unprocessed unless interest and penalty are included.

The office accepts no partial payments and no pro-rated amounts. If a parcel has more than one unpaid year, the oldest year is paid first, a rule the collector cites as RSMo 140.110. One check can cover several bills as long as you send every statement with it.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Pike County property tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay at the courthouse, by mail, by phone or online. Cash is taken in person only. Checks, money orders, cashier's checks and certified checks are accepted, and so are credit and debit cards with a convenience fee. A mailed payment counts as paid on its postmark date, and the receipt comes back by mail.

  • E-check: a flat 80 cents.
  • Visa, Mastercard and Discover: 2.35 percent of the total, minimum $1.00.
  • American Express: 2.95 percent of the total, minimum $1.00.
  • Automatic installments: bank draft under the free Pre-Pay program, described below.

sections.h2: How does Pike County assess a home, and when can I appeal?
sections.html:
The assessor values property as of January 1. Residential property is assessed at 19 percent of market value, agricultural at 12 percent of production value and other real estate at 32 percent. The office says real estate is reviewed every two years and that state law requires values to fall within 5 percent of market value.

The Pike County Assessor's calendar lists the dates that matter for a dispute:

Pike County assessment calendar from the county assessor's site
DateEvent
January 1Assessment date
March 1Personal property list due
June 15Notice of increased value mailed
July 1Totals go to the County Clerk
Third Monday in JulyBoard of Equalization hearings begin
September 30Deadline to appeal to the State Tax Commission

The assessor's page says staff will review a parcel and explain how the value was reached. If your taxes are escrowed, tell your lender as soon as a notice arrives so the monthly payment can be adjusted. Source: Pike County Assessor.

sections.h2: Can I dispute a Pike County bill without missing the payment deadline?
sections.html:
Yes. The State Tax Commission says taxes are due by December 31 whether or not an appeal is pending, but you may appeal without having paid. To pay under protest, send the full bill to the collector by December 31, write "paid under protest" on the check, and file a written statement of your grounds, including the fair market value you claim.

Appeals that start with the Board of Equalization must wait for its decision letter, and the next step is due within 30 days of that letter. A property held in a trust, LLC, corporation or estate must be appealed through an attorney. See the State Tax Commission guide.

sections.h2: What happens to a Pike County parcel with unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Real estate with a third year of delinquent tax must be offered at the August sale under RSMo 140.160. The sale takes place on the south side of the courthouse on the fourth Monday in August at 10 a.m. Listings run in a local paper for three consecutive weeks, and the last notice appears at least 15 days before the sale.

  • Bidding opens at the amount of all taxes, interest and charges.
  • The buyer pays at once and holds a Certificate of Purchase.
  • The owner keeps possession during the one-year redemption period (RSMo 140.310).
  • Money paid above the opening bid goes to the County Treasurer, and the owner of record can claim it. After three years it goes to the schools (RSMo 140.230).

The collector says a very high percentage of owners pay after the advertisement and before the sale. The office does not give legal advice, so a seller facing a listing should speak with a Missouri attorney.

sections.h2: Which Pike County programs can lower the cost?
sections.html:
Three programs are worth a call. The collector's Pre-Pay plan draws monthly amounts from a bank account at no charge, with the first installments based on the prior year's totals and the balance collected on November 15. It requires a yearly bill of at least $100 each for real estate and personal property, and a voided check is required to enroll.

The Senior Tax Freeze for 2027 takes applications from March 15 to June 30, 2027. The applicant must hold the deed to a primary residence in Pike County, be 62 by January 1 of the application year, be a Missouri resident and have no delinquent taxes. The state also runs the Property Tax Credit claim, which gives qualifying seniors and 100 percent disabled individuals up to $1,100 as owners, based on income and tax paid (Missouri Department of Revenue).

sections.h2: How do unpaid taxes affect selling a house in Pike County?
sections.html:
Plan to settle every open year before the sale, since the collector will not accept the current bill until older years are paid. The Pike office does not pro-rate a bill, so the split between buyer and seller is something the closing agent works out in the contract.

If you owe more than one year, call the collector in Bowling Green for exact payoff figures with interest. Ask the assessor for the legal description and the mailing address on file before you list, because the collector cannot fix either one.

faqs.q: What is the Pike County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: The deadline is December 31, judged by postmark. Pike County statements are mailed on the first day of November, and a payment postmarked after December 31 is returned unless interest and penalty are included.

faqs.q: Can I pay half of my Pike County bill now and half later?
faqs.a: No. The Pike County Collector accepts no partial payments, and payments for the wrong amount are returned. The free Pre-Pay installment plan is the way to spread the cost through the year.

faqs.q: How do I get a Pike County value corrected?
faqs.a: Call the Pike County Assessor at 573-324-3261 before the Board of Equalization hearings begin on the third Monday in July. If that fails, the State Tax Commission appeal is due by September 30 or within 30 days of the board's decision letter.

faqs.q: When is the Pike County tax sale?
faqs.a: The sale is on the fourth Monday in August at 10 a.m. on the south side of the courthouse. Only parcels with a third year of delinquent tax must be offered, and an owner can pay before the sale to remove the parcel.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the Pike County Senior Tax Freeze?
faqs.a: An applicant must hold the deed to a primary Pike County residence, be 62 by January 1 of the year applying, live in Missouri and owe no delinquent tax. Applications for 2027 run from March 15 to June 30, 2027.
